resources.string: Doorman watches which screen is open in apps you choose, so it can cover endless feeds while leaving messages, searches and individual videos alone.\n\nIt reads only the structure of the screen — the names of the elements in front of you. It never reads your messages, passwords or account details. Nothing is recorded, and nothing ever leaves your phone.
Messages get through. The feed does not.
Blocking is active for the screens you have switched on.
Doorman needs accessibility access to see which screen is open. Nothing you type or read is collected.
You asked Doorman to keep you out of here.
Need in anyway? Open Doorman and wait out a pass.
Everything is your choice. Switch off anything you would rather keep.
A blocked screen offers no way past it. If you really need in, you come here, wait, and get a short pass.
Leave this screen and the wait starts again.
You left, so the wait restarted.
Scrolling on from a single reel
Your time here is used up for now. It comes back on its own.
You have seen the one you opened. The rest is just the feed.
Apps redesign themselves, and when they do Doorman can stop recognising a screen. Capture a report and send it to the project so the rule can be fixed.
Doorman has not looked at anything yet.
You have 5 seconds to switch to the app that is misbehaving.
Report saved. It contains the screen\'s structure only — no text, no messages.
Nothing to capture. Is Doorman switched on?
Scrolling on from a single Short
Switching a block off waits before it takes effect, so a moment of impulse cannot undo a decision. Switching one on is immediate.
Leave this screen and the change is cancelled.
Stories row on the home feed
Keeping swiping from a video someone sent
Doorman follows your phone\'s language. Android 13 and later can also set a language just for Doorman, in Settings.
Any app on your phone. Games, shops, anything. Holding one here covers the whole app, because Doorman knows nothing about its insides.
Search for an app to hold. The ones you choose stay listed here.
Covers the entire app, every screen of it, including messages. Use this for an app Doorman has no detailed rules for, or when you want the whole thing shut rather than a part of it.

When someone sends you a Short, it plays. The block lands on the first swipe past it, so a link stays watchable without turning into a feed. Switch this off and a Short someone sent is blocked like any other.
The Shorts player itself, wherever you reach it from: the Shorts tab, a link, a channel. Videos you search for and ordinary videos are untouched.
The recommendations on the YouTube home tab. Search, subscriptions and any video you open still work.
The Subscriptions tab, which lists new videos from channels you follow. Off by default: for most people this is the deliberate part of YouTube rather than the endless part.

When someone sends you a reel, it plays. The block lands on the first swipe past it, so what a friend sent stays watchable without becoming a feed. Switch this off and a reel someone sent is blocked like any other.
Stories themselves, opened from anywhere: the home feed, a profile, a message. Off by default, because for many people stories are how friends talk to each other.
The Reels tab only. A reel opened from somewhere else — a message, a profile, a story — still plays. For those, use “Reels, wherever they open”.

Any reel playing full screen, no matter where you opened it from. Stricter than the Reels tab on its own. If “keep swiping from a reel someone sent” is also on, a reel sent to you still plays once before the block.
The scrolling posts on the home tab. The stories row along the top stays reachable unless you also block that, and messages, search and your profile are untouched.
Hides the row of stories along the top of the home feed, without blocking stories themselves. For when the row is the temptation but you still want to open stories from a message or from search.
The Explore grid behind the search tab. The search bar itself stays usable, so you can still look people up.

When you open a TikTok link from another app, that video plays and the block lands on the first swipe. TikTok drops shared links straight into the For You feed, so without this there is no way to watch what someone sent you.
The scrolling video feed: For You, Following, all of it. Your inbox, your profile and search still work.
The Spotlight tab, Snapchat\'s endless video feed. Chats, snaps, the camera and the map are untouched.
The Discover grid of publisher content on the Stories tab. Your friends\' stories along the top stay reachable unless you also block that row.
Hides the row of friends\' stories at the top of the Stories tab, without blocking stories themselves.
Not at this hour. You set this one aside.
Set the hours it is closed. A block that ends earlier than it starts runs through the night.
Runs through midnight. The days you pick are the mornings it ends on: with weekdays, Friday night is free and Sunday night is not.
